title: Duplicate charges from Stripe webhook retries
content:
User: Our billing-api keeps charging some customers twice. I traced it to Stripe retrying failed webhooks — every retry re-runs the handler and processes the same payment event again. Right now roughly 3 customers a day get double-charged.

Assistant: The handler isn't idempotent. Options: (1) use Stripe's idempotency keys on the charge call, (2) a processed_events table with a unique constraint on the Stripe event id, (3) make the handler side-effect-free and reconcile later.

User: Which is simplest to ship this week?

Assistant: Option 2 — check the Stripe event id against processed_events inside the same Postgres transaction as the charge insert. Retries then become no-ops. You'll want a migration for the unique index and integration tests that replay the same event twice.

User: OK, going with the processed_events check. So today retries re-process payments and double-charge customers; after this change retries should be safely ignored. Draft the migration and the test plan for me.

title: Feed API p95 at 800ms — Redis cache or materialized view?
content:
User: The mobile-backend feed endpoint is slow — p95 latency is around 800ms. Profiling shows an N+1 pattern: every feed request re-joins activities, likes, and comments for the whole friend graph. What are my options?

Assistant: Two realistic ones: (1) a Redis cache in front of the composed feed with a short TTL and write-through invalidation on new posts and comments, (2) a Postgres materialized view refreshed on a schedule. Given the bursty comment write pattern, option 1 gives better staleness behavior with less schema surgery.

User: Let's do Redis. What TTL?

Assistant: 60 seconds covers the hot path; invalidate explicitly on post and comment writes so authors see their own content immediately. Today every feed request recomputes the full join — with the cache, only the first request per minute pays that cost.

User: OK — Redis, 60s TTL, explicit invalidation on writes. Sketch the module boundaries and the load test we should run before shipping.

title: Codex session: idempotent Stripe webhook handler in billing-api
content:
User: Implement the idempotency fix we designed for the Stripe webhook handler in billing-api: check the Stripe event id against a processed_events table inside the same Postgres transaction as the charge, add the unique index migration, and add tests that replay duplicate events.

Codex: Added migration 0042_processed_events with a unique index on stripe_event_id. Updated src/webhooks/stripe.ts so the processed_events insert and the charge insert happen in one Postgres transaction — a duplicate event id now rolls the whole retry back as a no-op.

Codex: Added 4 integration tests, including one that replays the exact same webhook payload three times and asserts a single charge. Full suite passes: 142 passed, 0 failed.

Session summary: duplicate webhook retries are now deduplicated at the transaction boundary; nothing is double-charged on retry.

content:

Assistant: 1) "Sadly I can't join the sync — could you share the notes afterwards?" 2) "I'll have to skip this one — mind forwarding the notes?" 3) "Can't make it this time, but I'd love to catch up on the notes!"

User: Second one. Thanks.

title: Migrating CI from CircleCI to GitHub Actions — strategy
content:
User: platform-infra pays about $1.9k/month for CircleCI across 18 jobs and the bill keeps climbing. I want to move to GitHub Actions. Cloud runners or self-hosted?

Assistant: With your existing k8s cluster, self-hosted runners on spot nodes cost roughly a quarter of cloud runners at your job volume. The catch: runner registration tokens need infra approval, and you should migrate job-by-job while keeping CircleCI running in parallel.

User: Self-hosted it is. Today every CI run happens on CircleCI; the goal is all 18 jobs on GitHub Actions with the CircleCI project archived. Give me a migration order that keeps deploys safe.

Assistant: Migrate lint, unit, and integration jobs first — cheap to verify — and leave the 6 deploy jobs for last since they need the runner tokens. Keep both CIs green on the same commit until the final cutover.

title: Codex session: Redis cache layer for the feed endpoint
content:
User: Add the Redis cache layer to the mobile-backend feed endpoint we discussed: wrap the feed query with a 60s TTL cache and invalidate on new posts and comments.

Codex: Created src/feed/cache.ts exposing FeedCache with get-or-compute semantics, wired it into the feed handler, and added invalidation hooks on post-create and comment-create. Kept the Postgres query untouched behind the cache boundary.

Codex: Load test at 10x production traffic: p95 latency dropped from 810ms to 90ms with a 97% cache hit rate. All 218 tests pass.

Session summary: the feed endpoint now serves from cache except on the first request per TTL window; feed latency is no longer dominated by the activity join.

title: Codex session: GitHub Actions workflow migration — 12 of 18 jobs moved
content:
User: Start the CircleCI to GitHub Actions migration for platform-infra: scaffold .github/workflows and move the lint, unit, and integration jobs first.

Codex: Created .github/workflows/ci.yml plus two reusable workflow files; migrated 12 of 18 jobs (lint, 4 unit jobs, 7 integration jobs). All migrated jobs are green on GitHub Actions while CircleCI still runs the full set in parallel.

Codex: The remaining 6 deploy jobs need self-hosted runner registration tokens, which require infra approval. Blocked on that — nothing further can be done from here.

Session summary: 12/18 jobs now run on GitHub Actions; the migration is on hold pending runner tokens.
